name: Audiovisual Media Services Directive
impact_assessment: none for the 2010 codification; SWD(2016) 168 for the 2018 amendment
evidence_rating: thin: Commission evaluation and monitoring reports with conflicting figures; no independent causal studies of quotas or other rules found
summary: The AVMS Directive lets TV and streaming services operate EU-wide under one country's rules and requires them to promote European works. The Commission's 2016 evaluation found the single-country rule effective but admitted little hard data. Member States report European works at about two-thirds of TV and streaming content, yet an independent check found only 35-38%, and no study measures whether the quotas boosted European production.

indicators.objective: The 2009 proposal was a codification with no indicators; monitoring is through biennial Member State reports on European works (Arts 13, 16, 17). The 2016 evaluation found no effective monitoring system

indicators.indicator: Majority of transmission time for European works; 10% for independent works
indicators.evidence: Member States report 68-69% European works on TV (2020-21), down from 72.6% (2019); an independent sample study found only 38%, and under 3% independent European works vs 40-41% reported.

indicators.indicator: At least 30% European works in VOD catalogues, with prominence
indicators.evidence: Member States report 63-64% (2020-21); independent snapshot of 1,062 services (2023) found 35%; methods differ and data incomplete.
2016 evaluation: perceived as effective, brought legal certainty and economies of scale; robust economic data lacking.

indicators.objective: Protection of minors on video-sharing platforms
indicators.evidence: Costs and benefits not quantified; no outcome measurement found.

literature.citation: European Commission (2016), Ex-post REFIT evaluation of the Audiovisual Media Services Directive 2010/13/EU (executive summary SWD(2016) 171), SWD(2016) 170
literature.title: Ex-post REFIT evaluation of the Audiovisual Media Services Directive 2010/13/EU (executive summary SWD(2016) 171)
literature.method: REFIT evaluation (three public consultations, studies, monitoring reports)
literature.outcomes: single market; cultural diversity; pluralism; costs
literature.headline: Country-of-origin principle effective; Directive enhanced cultural diversity on TV but less so on demand; partly effective on media freedom; robust economic data and compliance-cost data lacking; no effective monitoring system
literature.summary_plain: The 2016 evaluation found the rules let broadcasters operate EU-wide under one country's law, but admitted there was little hard data on their effects.

literature.citation: European Commission (2016), Impact assessment for the amendment of Directive 2010/13/EU (executive summary SWD(2016) 169), SWD(2016) 168
literature.title: Impact assessment for the amendment of Directive 2010/13/EU (executive summary SWD(2016) 169)
literature.headline: Preferred options: obligations on video-sharing platforms for minors and hate speech, stronger European-works rules for on-demand services, independent regulators; costs mainly on on-demand and video-sharing services, mitigated by existing practice; not quantified
literature.summary_plain: The Commission proposed extending the rules to video-sharing platforms and on-demand services, without putting numbers on costs or benefits.

literature.citation: European Commission (2024), Report on the application of Articles 13, 16 and 17 of Directive 2010/13/EU for 2020-2021 (with SWD(2024) 149), COM(2024) 261
literature.title: Report on the application of Articles 13, 16 and 17 of Directive 2010/13/EU for 2020-2021 (with SWD(2024) 149)
literature.method: Member State reports plus independent sample study
literature.headline: VOD: Member States report 63-64% European works, independent study of 1,062 services finds 35%; TV: reported 68-69% vs 38% in the study, independent productions reported 40-41% vs under 3% in the study; SVOD revenues EUR 6.7bn (2019) to EUR 11.7bn (2021)
literature.summary_plain: Countries report that European works make up about two-thirds of TV and streaming content, but an independent check found only about 35-38%.
literature.quality: official data inconsistent with independent sample
